issues.legal_issue: A signatory to a will may qualify as an attesting witness without being labelled as one when the evidence establishes the required witnessing and signing.
material_facts: The will bore the signatures of three people beneath the testatrix’s thumb-mark, although it did not describe them as attesting witnesses.
A signatory testified that he and the other signatories saw the testatrix place her thumb-mark on the will and signed it in her presence.
issues.conclusion: The signatory’s evidence established that he was an attesting witness, and the objection that no attesting witness had proved execution failed.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 63(c) of the Indian Succession Act, 1975, an attesting witness signs in the executant’s presence after seeing execution or receiving the executant’s personal acknowledgment of it. Section 68 of the Indian Evidence Act requires an available attesting witness to be called to prove execution of a document required by law to be attested. The label given to a signatory is not decisive; the evidence must establish the acts constituting attestation.

predicates.will_probate_proceeding: A party sought probate of a will whose execution had to be proved.
predicates.signatory_saw_execution: A signatory saw the testator execute the will or received the testator’s personal acknowledgment of its execution.
predicates.signatory_signed_in_executant_presence: The signatory signed the will while the testator was present.

issues.definition: When a will is being proved and a signatory witnessed its execution and signed in the testator’s presence, that signatory qualifies as an attesting witness.

issues.legal_issue: A will may be proved despite suspicious circumstances when the propounder satisfactorily explains them and establishes the testator’s sound and disposing state of mind.
material_facts: The testatrix was over eighty and died five days after executing the will, which disinherited her only son.
The testatrix and her son had a long history of serious estrangement and litigation, and she had previously excluded him from gifts and testamentary dispositions.

The will benefited other members of the family, while the advocate who prepared or witnessed it had no interest in its outcome; another person accused of participating in a forgery stood to lose by the will.
Evidence supported that the will was read to the testatrix, that she was in a sound state of mind, and that the signatories witnessed its execution.
The son did not testify to support his accusation of forgery.
issues.conclusion: The propounder discharged the burden of proving the will and satisfactorily explained the suspicious circumstances; the will was established as the testatrix’s last will, made while she was of sound and disposing mind and memory.
issues.legal_principle: The burden of proof rests on the party propounding a will, who must satisfy the court that it is the last will of a free and capable testator. Ordinarily, proof of the testator’s signature or mark and due attestation discharges the burden, subject to the requirement in section 68 of the Indian Evidence Act to call an available attesting witness. Where suspicious circumstances surround execution, the propounder must remove the suspicion with satisfactory evidence and an explanation sufficient to satisfy a prudent mind; mathematical proof is not required. The Court applied the approach in H. Venkatachala Iyengar v. B.N. Thimmajamma, and referred to Jarman on Wills and Harmes v. Hinkson on the assessment of testamentary proof.

rule.if: will_probate_proceeding and suspicious_execution_circumstances and propounder_satisfactorily_explains_suspicion and testator_sound_and_disposing_mind

predicates.will_probate_proceeding: A party sought to establish a will in probate proceedings.
predicates.suspicious_execution_circumstances: Circumstances surrounding execution gave reason to doubt the will’s due execution or authenticity.
predicates.propounder_satisfactorily_explains_suspi: The person propounding the will presented evidence and explanations that satisfactorily addressed the suspicious circumstances.
predicates.testator_sound_and_disposing_mind: The evidence established that the testator had a sound and disposing state of mind and memory when making the will.

issues.definition: In probate proceedings, a will is proved when suspicious circumstances are satisfactorily explained and the testator is shown to have had a sound and disposing mind.

issues.legal_issue: A transferee who acquired an interest in estate property during pending probate litigation could not invalidate the grant by objecting that no citation had been issued to that transferee before the proceedings began.
material_facts: A purchaser acquired some of the property covered by the will while an appeal in the probate proceedings was pending.
The purchaser argued that the grant of probate was invalid because the purchaser had not received a citation.

The Court assumed, without deciding, that a purchaser with an interest acquired from the heirs might otherwise be entitled to citation, but observed that no citation could have been issued to this purchaser before the probate proceedings commenced.
issues.conclusion: The purchaser’s citation objection did not invalidate the grant of probate; the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: The Court assumed without affirming the proposition that a purchaser who acquires an interest in the estate from the heirs may be entitled to citation in testamentary proceedings. It distinguished a transferee pendente lite, whose interest was acquired while the probate appeal was pending and who therefore could not have been cited before the proceedings commenced. The Court referred to Banwarilal Shriniwas v. Kumari Kusum Bai but did not adopt its proposition as a definitive holding.

predicates.probate_proceeding: A court was considering proceedings to establish a will and grant probate.
predicates.transferee_acquired_interest_after_proce: A transferee acquired an interest in estate property while the probate proceedings or their appeal were pending.
predicates.transferee_could_not_be_cited_before_pro: The transferee acquired the interest only after the proceedings began, so no citation could have been issued to that transferee beforehand.

issues.definition: When a transferee acquires an interest only after probate proceedings have begun and could not have been cited earlier, the absence of prior citation does not invalidate the grant.
